export: 1920×1080 30 fps, H.264 High, CRF 23, maxrate 6 Mbps (bufsize 12M), AAC 160 k, +faststart; watermark top-left x 48 y 40 h 56 on every frame except the end card (state/brand.md)
rules: PRODUCTION_SPEC §1/§3/§9 scaled to 16:9: real Apple product ≥ 60 % of runtime, ≥ 12 distinct real images (A–P, Z), a detailed 2-D object in every scene, every number shown. Chapter cards at each chapter start (big title, 1.5 s, same style each time). Flat light backgrounds; MacBook is silver/space black → paper/mint/lavender/blush/marigold OK. No Apple logo drawn by us, no app brand logos (text tiles only). Audio LOCKED (narrate.py + mix.sh) with the voice from handoff/sow015-apple-macbook-pro-proled-voice. Length ~9–10 min.
official_clips: V1 Apple Newsroom OLED-technology autoplay (assets_sources.md): ≤ 3 s per use, ≤ 2 uses, muted, our graphic on top, credit 'Apple' in description (already credited as Apple Newsroom).
palette_for_this_video: paper #FAF8F5 main; mint = tests that pass; blush = the catch/wobble/crack; lavender = name/body; marigold = brightness + price chapter cards; ember accent for all numbers
assets: assets_sources.md (A–P Apple Newsroom zips, Z = M6 MacBook Pro newsroom image, V1 clip)
new_objects: miniLedStack and oledStack (screen.js) — add both to render/kit/OBJECTS.md. Reuse everything else from the library.
chapters: Chapter starts in script.md headers are estimates (133 wpm). Write the real start time of each [CHn] in qa.md → 'chapters:' so the description can be corrected before upload.

scenes.anchor: Since nineteen eighty-four, you couldn't touch a Mac screen.
scenes.object: calendar flips 1984 → 2026; finger icon (arrowPointer variant) taps the screen, ripple rings

scenes.anchor: Now you can.
scenes.object: speechBubble-style tap ripple + tick

scenes.anchor: It's called the MacBook Pro with PROLED X D R Display.
scenes.object: name label on leader line: 'PROLED XDR DISPLAY'; small pill '14" · 16"'

scenes.anchor: It's Apple's first Mac with Touch.
scenes.object: questionStamp swaps to '1st' badge on the screen corner

scenes.anchor: It went on sale on November sixth. It starts at twenty-eight ninety-nine.
scenes.object: calendar 'NOV 6 2026' + priceTag swings in '$2,899'

scenes.anchor: Today, we'll see how this screen works
scenes.object: chapter strip: 4 tiles (SCREEN · TOUCH · TESTS · INSIDE) light up in order, then a SPEC/WRECK see-saw wobbles

scenes.anchor: Okay, so first, the screen.
scenes.object: chapter card 'HOW TANDEM OLED WORKS'; screen object outline

scenes.anchor: Picture the old MacBook Pro screen. It's mini-LED.
scenes.image: none (diagram scene; product B small in corner 25%)
scenes.object: NEW screenPath cross-section 'miniLedStack': backlight row of tiny LEDs (dots) in zones → LCD layer → glass; labels 'LED ZONES', 'PIXELS FILTER'
scenes.new_object: miniLedStack (screen.js): layered cross-section, LED dots in zone groups, light rays upward

scenes.anchor: So a white star on a black sky? You can get a little glow around it.
scenes.bg: ink-free dark panel inside a paper frame (screen object only)
scenes.object: screen object: black sky with one white star; zone behind lights up → soft halo ring around star, callout 'BLOOMING'

scenes.anchor: Now picture OLED. There's no light behind anything.
scenes.object: 'oledStack' cross-section: single layer of self-lit pixels, each pixel a small sun; backlight row slides out (strike-through)
scenes.new_object: oledStack (screen.js): pixel row where each pixel can glow or switch off; option layers=2 for tandem

scenes.anchor: Want black? The pixel just switches off. Totally off.
scenes.object: star-sky screen again: halo gone, pixels around the star at 0 (toggle OFF)

scenes.anchor: Apple didn't use one OLED layer. It used two.
scenes.object: oledStack layers=2: second pixel layer drops onto the first, counter '1 → 2'
scenes.clip: V1 OLED technology, ≤3 s, muted, under the stack graphic

scenes.anchor: Two layers can share the work, and get brighter together.
scenes.object: two stacked suns each half-filled → combined gauge fills higher

scenes.anchor: Ten million to one contrast. Ten million!
scenes.object: counter rolls to 10,000,000:1; bars chart (white bar vs near-zero black bar)

scenes.anchor: Notebookcheck measured the contrast as infinite.
scenes.object: reviewCard 'Notebookcheck — measured' with '∞ : 1'

scenes.anchor: It also runs up to a hundred and twenty hertz.
scenes.object: gauge needle sweeps 10 → 120 Hz

scenes.anchor: And it covers P three and Adobe R G B color
scenes.object: colour-gamut triangle (CIE horseshoe outline) with P3 + AdobeRGB triangles; ring '98% P3 (measured)'

scenes.anchor: For photo and video work? That's a serious screen.
scenes.object: tick badge

scenes.anchor: Now, the part everyone's talking about. Touch.
scenes.object: chapter card 'TOUCH'; finger tap ripple on screen

scenes.anchor: Would you actually reach up and poke your laptop?
scenes.object: questionStamp

scenes.anchor: You can swipe to scroll. Pinch to zoom. Drag and drop.
scenes.object: gesture row: 3 hand-drawn gesture glyphs (swipe arrow, pinch arrows, drag path) appear one per phrase

scenes.anchor: Double-tap a window, and it fills the screen. Flick it, and it tiles to the side.
scenes.object: ui window on a screen: double-tap → expands; flick → snaps to right half

scenes.anchor: Apple's apps are tuned for fingers. So are Word, Zoom and Lightroom.
scenes.object: appTile row: plain lettered tiles 'Word' 'Zoom' 'Lightroom' (text only, NO brand logos)

scenes.anchor: And there's a newly designed hinge
scenes.object: hinge arc callout with angle marks; lock icon

scenes.anchor: Macworld loved it. They said it's so good it can replace the trackpad.
scenes.object: reviewCard 'Macworld' quote 'can replace the trackpad'; trackpad outline gets slash

scenes.anchor: Notebookcheck was cooler on it.
scenes.object: reviewCard 'Notebookcheck' quote 'more of a gimmick'

scenes.anchor: Notebookcheck says the screen wobbles slightly when you touch it.
scenes.object: screen outline rocks ±3° on tap with motion lines

scenes.anchor: it turns on extra video stabilization while you touch the screen.
scenes.object: camera lens with stabiliser crosshair; wobble line flattens

scenes.anchor: Touch is real, and it's good. But it's a bonus.
scenes.object: bars: 'Screen' tall, 'Touch' short labelled BONUS

scenes.anchor: Okay. Brightness. This is where it gets interesting.
scenes.object: chapter card 'THE FINE PRINT'; sun object

scenes.anchor: Apple's press release says up to two thousand nits, H D R and S D R.
scenes.object: speechBubble 'up to 2000 nits peak HDR and SDR' (Apple Newsroom)

scenes.anchor: But Apple's own spec page is more careful.
scenes.object: magnifier over a spec-sheet card; lines highlight

scenes.anchor: It says a thousand nits sustained, full screen. Two thousand nits peak, for H D R content.
scenes.object: two bars: 1,000 sustained / 2,000 peak (HDR)

scenes.anchor: two thousand peak only outdoors. And a footnote says, under twenty-five degrees.
scenes.object: sun + thermometer with mark at 25 °C, footnote '³'

scenes.anchor: Notebookcheck measured H D R peak at about two thousand and eighty-five nits.
scenes.object: gauge needle to 2,085; tick vs claim line 2,000

scenes.anchor: With the light sensor off, they measured six hundred nits.
scenes.object: bars: 600 (sensor off) vs 1,025 (sensor on) vs 2,000 claim (dashed)

scenes.anchor: But you'll mostly see it on H D R video, or out in the sun. Not in your spreadsheet.
scenes.object: screen split: HDR movie frame bright vs spreadsheet grid dim

scenes.anchor: Next up, Apple's other big number. Up to twenty-four hours of battery.
scenes.object: chapter card 'BATTERY'; battery with cells fills; counter 24 h

scenes.anchor: Apple tested pre-production machines, in September.
scenes.object: calendar 'SEPT 2026' + brightness slider at 8 clicks from bottom + keyboard backlight toggle OFF

scenes.anchor: Macworld looped a video on the sixteen-inch M5 Max.
scenes.object: clockRing loops; reviewCard 'Macworld'; bars 22 h claim vs ~24 h measured

scenes.anchor: Notebookcheck tested the fourteen-inch.
scenes.object: bars Wi-Fi: 14 h claim vs 16 h 37 m measured (tick)

scenes.anchor: Local video ran nineteen hours, twenty-one minutes.
scenes.object: bars video: 22 h claim vs 19 h 21 m (short, amber)

scenes.anchor: the sixteen-inch battery isn't bigger. It's about a hundred watt-hours
scenes.object: two battery objects same size labelled '~100 Wh' MINI-LED / OLED, equals sign

scenes.anchor: Now, the body. Pick one up, and you'd feel it.
scenes.object: chapter card 'THE BODY'; scale object
